headline: The AI trade cracked in New York, not Seoul: SOXX -8.2% in a single session, and gold was sold alongside it — the signature of forced de-grossing, not rotation.
summary: Yesterday's break was in Asia. Today it arrived onshore and it was violent. SOXX fell 8.2% and SMH 7.0% in one session, taking SMH to -14.2% on the month and SOXX to -17.1%, with SMH/SPY at z=-2.31 and acceleration -2.48. The casualty list is the entire AI capex chain: AMD -10.9%, ASML -6.6%, TSM -5.9%, AVGO -5.5%, MU -5.3%, ORCL -6.4%, NVDA -4.2%, PLTR -6.3%. Press reports tie the catalyst to disappointing chip guidance, with Intel the epicentre. NDX -3.5% versus SPX -1.8%; QQQ/SPY is z=-2.37 with acceleration -2.63. This was not a general equity liquidation — equal-weight fell only 0.8% and RSP/SPY rose 1.0% to z=3.0 with acceleration 3.55, the single largest positive score on the entire board. Energy actually gained: XLE +1.9%, XOP +2.1%, XOM +2.2% and CVX +1.8%, both at the 100th percentile of their 52-week range.

The tell that this is deleveraging rather than rotation is the precious metals tape. Gold fell 3.6% to 3,884.9 — the 0th percentile of the year, 14.1% below its 200-day — while silver dropped 5.9% (z=-2.03, -18.2% on the month) and platinum 4.0% (z=-1.88). GDXJ -5.9%, GDX -5.2%, COPX -5.2%, FCX -5.5%. Hedges and winners are being sold to fund losses. Gold/silver jumped another 2.4% to z=2.02. Risk appetite broke with it: high-beta/low-vol collapsed 5.2% in a day, -16.2% on the month at z=-2.57 and acceleration -2.64; growth/value sits at the 0th percentile of its 52-week range; ARKK -6.1%, IPO -6.3%, MTUM -4.8% at z=-2.05. COIN -10.6% and MSTR -7.8% while bitcoin itself only lost 1.2% — equity proxies are bearing the margin pain, not the underlying.

Rates gave no relief worth owning. Yields fell again — 5y -7bp to 4.71, 10y -4bp to 4.94, 2y -5bp to 4.56 — extending a one-month duration rally that is now statistically absurd: DGS5 -38bp at acceleration -2.56, DGS10 -35bp at -2.49, 10y real yield -33bp at -2.43, IEF +3.1% on the month at acceleration 2.27. That rally is happening against an inflation composite of -48, WTI at 102.95 (+13.9% on the month, +79.3% YTD), DBC at the 96th percentile, oil/gold at a fresh 100th-percentile reading after +4.7% today, and the 5-year breakeven turning up at 2.46. The 30-year mortgage is 7.24%, up 21bp on the month even as the 10-year fell 35bp. MOVE rose 7.1% back to 100.2. A two-sigma bond rally into accelerating energy inflation is a positioning event with an expiry date.

Credit still refuses to sign off. HYG/IEF fell another 0.7% to -2.3% on the month at z=-1.69 even as HYG itself barely moved. VIX +12.9% to 19.42, VIX3M +7.3% to 20.78, the term structure up 5.2% to 0.935 and turning up, SKEW at 149.8. And the periphery keeps bleeding under a flat dollar headline (DXY -0.1%): USD/BRL +1.8% today and +7.7% on the week, EWZ -23.8% in five sessions, Bovespa -18.1%, USD/MXN at the 100th percentile of the year, ARGT -9.1% on the week, TUR -12.6% on the month, EEM/SPY at z=-1.89. The risk regime deteriorated to -20 from -14. What is still working is narrow and defensive: XLP +1.4% (z=2.87, acc 2.78), XLV +0.5% at the 100th percentile with z=2.31, LLY +3.2% and +22.5% on the month, WMT +1.9%, COST +1.6%, LMT at z=3.26 with acceleration 3.31, UPS +15.8% on the month, and DJT green on a -1.8% tape.

good.text: Breadth absorbed the mega-cap shock. Equal-weight fell only 0.8% against SPX -1.8%; RSP/SPY rose 1.0% to z=3.0 with acceleration 3.55 — the biggest positive reading anywhere on the sheet — and SPW is +4.9% on the month at the 91st percentile.
Energy equities went up on a down-3.5% Nasdaq day: XLE +1.9% (+13.9% month, rel. strength +14.9%, 100th percentile), XOP +2.1%, OIH +0.9%, XOM +2.2% and CVX +1.8% both at 52-week highs.

Yields fell across the curve again — 5y 4.71 (-38bp on the month), 10y 4.94 (-35bp), 10y real yield 2.60 (-33bp) — and TLT is +5.6% on the month. Financing costs for everything outside housing are easing fast.
Copper/gold punched to the 100th percentile, +2.6% today and +7.0% on the month, with copper down just 1.1%. Global cyclical demand is not what broke today.

Logistics and healthcare are compounding through the mess: DJT +0.5% and IYT/SPY acceleration 2.28, UPS +15.8% on the month at z=2.06, FDX +9.9%; XLV +9.8% at z=2.31 and the 100th percentile, LLY +22.5%, IBB at the 99.6th percentile.
Loan and IG credit cash markets are not cracking: BKLN at the 97th percentile of the year, LQD +2.5% on the month with acceleration 1.70, HYG only -0.2% on an 8% semis washout.

bad.text: The semiconductor complex is in outright liquidation and accelerating downward: SOXX -8.2% in a day (-17.1% month, acc -2.01), SMH -7.0% (-14.2%), AMD -10.9% (acc -1.91), ASML -6.6%, TSM -5.9%, AVGO -5.5%, MU -5.3%. SMH/SPY z=-2.31, acceleration -2.48.

Risk appetite is gone, and the deterioration is speeding up. High-beta/low-vol -5.2% in one session, -16.2% on the month at z=-2.57 with acceleration -2.64; growth/value at the 0th percentile of the year; ARKK -6.1%, IPO -6.3%, MTUM z=-2.05.
Gold -3.6% to the 0th percentile, silver -5.9% at z=-2.03, platinum -4.0%, GDXJ -5.9%. Hedges being sold on a down equity day is a de-grossing signature, not a macro view. Gold/silver z=2.02.

The inflation composite is -48, the worst number on the board. WTI 102.95 (+79.3% YTD), DBC at the 96th percentile, oil/gold at a 100th-percentile high after +4.7%, 5y breakevens turning up at 2.46, and the 30-year mortgage stuck at 7.24% despite a 35bp drop in the 10-year.

Credit and vol are both refusing to confirm the equal-weight bid: HYG/IEF -2.3% on the month at z=-1.69, VIX +12.9% to 19.42, VIX3M +7.3%, term structure +5.2% to 0.935 and turning up, SKEW 149.8, MOVE back above 100.
LatAm is dislocating under a flat dollar: USD/BRL +7.7% on the week, EWZ -23.8%, Bovespa -18.1% (z=-2.05), USD/MXN at the 100th percentile, ARGT -9.1%, TUR -12.6% on the month, EEM/SPY z=-1.89.

trades.name: Equal-weight over the Nasdaq
trades.line: Long RSP vs short QQQ — breadth z=3.0 vs QQQ/SPY z=-2.37
trades.expr: Dollar-neutral: long RSP, short QQQ in equal notional. Size 2-3% of book per leg; roll monthly.
trades.thesis: The index decline is a mega-cap AI problem, not an economy problem. Equal-weight lost 0.8% on a day the Nasdaq 100 lost 3.5%, and the money leaving semis is landing in staples, health care, energy and insurance — all equal-weight-heavy.
trades.trigger: RSP/SPY +1.0% today to z=3.0 with acceleration 3.55, the largest positive score on the sheet; QQQ/SPY -1.7% to z=-2.37 with acceleration -2.63 and SPW +4.9% on the month at the 91st percentile.
trades.stop: RSP/SPY gives back the entire October gain (below -1% on the month) or QQQ/SPY reclaims its 200-day, i.e. a V-shaped mega-cap recovery.
trades.target: A further 6-8% of relative outperformance, taking RSP/SPY toward the top decile of its 52-week range.

trades.name: Software over semis
trades.line: Long IGV vs short SMH — IGV/SMH z=2.07, acc 2.36
trades.expr: Long IGV, short SMH, equal notional. Alternatively short SOXX against IGV for cleaner borrow.
trades.thesis: The AI trade is being repriced from hardware capex to software monetisation. Semis carry the inventory, guidance and China risk; software carries recurring revenue and is 11.0% above its 200-day while SMH has given the entire bounce back.
trades.trigger: IGV/SMH +3.8% today to z=2.07 with acceleration 2.36 and +14.2% on the month, while SOXX fell 8.2% in a session and SMH/SPY accelerated to -2.48.
trades.stop: IGV/SMH back below its 200-day (roughly -8% from here) or IGV breaking its month-to-date low on its own, which would mean the whole tech complex is going, not just hardware.
trades.target: Another 10-12% in the ratio; IGV/SMH back toward the 60th percentile of its 52-week range.

trades.name: Energy equity, the only up-tape
trades.line: Long XOP/XLE — green on a -1.8% SPX day, 100th pctile
trades.expr: Core long XLE, higher-beta sleeve in XOP; add XOM and CVX as the quality anchors. Fund by trimming materials/XME.
trades.thesis: Crude at 102.95 is +13.9% on the month and +79.3% YTD, and energy equities are the one group with positive absolute, relative and acceleration scores. Oil/gold at a 52-week high says the cash flow is real, not a hedge bid.
trades.trigger: XLE +1.9% and XOP +2.1% on a day SPX fell 1.8%; XLE relative strength +14.9% on the month with acceleration 1.51; XOM +2.2% and CVX +1.8% at the 100th percentile; OIH acceleration 1.31.
trades.stop: WTI closes below 92 (roughly its 200-day plus a small buffer) or XLE's one-month relative strength flips negative.

trades.name: Fade the two-sigma duration rally
trades.line: Short IEF / pay 5y — -38bp on the month vs CPI tape
trades.expr: Short IEF outright, or buy 3-month TLT puts ~5% out of the money. Belly is the cleanest expression: pay 5y swaps.
trades.thesis: A 35-38bp rally across the 5s-10s sector with acceleration below -2.4 is a positioning flush, not a disinflation signal. Breakevens are turning up, crude is +14% on the month and mortgages have gone the wrong way. Something has to give, and it is the nominal yield.
trades.trigger: DGS5 -38bp on the month at acceleration -2.56 and DGS10 -35bp at -2.49, against a 5y breakeven turning up at 2.46 (+10bp on the month), DBC at the 96th percentile, and the 30-year mortgage at 7.24%, +21bp on the month. MOVE reaccelerated 7.1% to 100.2.
trades.stop: 10y breaks 4.70, or crude loses 15% from 102.95 and the 5y breakeven rolls back under 2.35 — then the bond rally is a real disinflation call.

trades.name: Gold over silver into the liquidation
trades.line: Long GLD vs short SLV — gold/silver z=2.02, +13.5% 1m
trades.expr: Long GLD, short an equal-notional silver position (SLV or COMEX silver); keep gold leg slightly larger to carry the de-grossing beta.
trades.thesis: This is a margin-driven unwind of crowded precious metals longs, and the industrial/levered leg always goes first. Silver is -18.2% on the month at z=-2.03 and platinum -15.7%; gold is -7.2%. The ratio is the cleanest way to own the liquidation without calling the bottom.
trades.trigger: Silver -5.9% and platinum -4.0% today versus gold -3.6%; gold/silver +2.4% to 79.07 at z=2.02 with acceleration 1.11 and the 87th percentile; GDXJ -5.9% and GDX -5.2% confirming the leveraged leg is where the pain is.
trades.stop: Gold/silver back below 72 (roughly its 200-day), or silver reclaims 55 — that would mean the squeeze is over and the industrial bid is back.

trades.name: Developed ex-US over EM
trades.line: Long EFA vs short EEM — EFA/SPY +0.8% today, EEM z=-1.85
trades.expr: Long EFA, short EEM, equal notional. Overlay: short BRL via USD/BRL forwards if you want the sharper edge.
trades.thesis: EM is carrying two unrelated shocks at once — a Korea/Taiwan semiconductor break and a LatAm funding scare — while Europe and the UK are quietly turning up with a flat dollar. The index composition makes EEM a leveraged short on exactly today's two losing themes.
trades.trigger: EEM -2.7% to z=-1.85 versus EFA -0.9%; EFA/SPY +0.8% with acceleration 0.92 while EEM/SPY is -7.8% on the month at z=-1.89. EWY -5.5% and EWT -4.6% on the semis break; USD/BRL +7.7% on the week with EWZ -23.8% and Bovespa -18.1% (z=-2.05); USD/MXN at the 100th percentile.
trades.stop: EFA/EEM gives back 4% of relative performance, or USD/BRL settles back under 5.10 and KOSPI reclaims its 200-day together — that is an EM all-clear.

trades.name: Crypto equity beta, not crypto
trades.line: Short COIN — -10.6% vs BTC -1.2%, 1st pctile of the year
trades.expr: Short COIN outright, or buy Jan puts 15% out of the money. Hedge with a small long IBIT to isolate the equity-beta short if you don't want spot exposure.
trades.thesis: The listed crypto complex is de-rating far faster than the asset it tracks. That gap is leverage and fee-revenue compression, and it widens when high-beta equity is being liquidated.
trades.trigger: COIN -10.6% today and -23.0% on the month, at the 1.2nd percentile of its 52-week range and 19.7% below its 200-day, while bitcoin fell only 1.2% and is still 4.9% above its 200-day. MSTR -7.8%. High-beta/low-vol collapsed 5.2% the same session.
trades.stop: COIN reclaims 170, or bitcoin breaks 85,000 to the upside and drags the complex with it.
